sourceWitness.author: Dom Prosper Guéranger
sourceWitness.work: Explication des prières de la sainte messe
sourceWitness.limitation: HTML transcription has known textual errors; do not treat its Latin as the normative 1962 Mass witness or its symbolic interpretation as rubrical authority.

focusedSix.prayer: Credo: maker of visible and invisible
focusedSix.interpretation: Creator of both bodily and angelic spiritual beings; anti-dualist reading is attributed to Guéranger; compare Catechism §§325–327 without treating the latter as an 1885 original.

focusedSix.prayer: Credo: for us and for salvation
focusedSix.interpretation: God the Word assumes our humanity for deliverance from sin and salvation; the liturgical genuflection occurs at Incarnatus, a later distinct clause, and must not be moved to this cue.

focusedSix.prayer: Deus qui humanae substantiae water/wine prayer
focusedSix.interpretation: Water/wine as representation of Christ's humanity and divinity, and of humanity joined to Christ; reciprocity of participating in divine nature / Christ participating in humanity. One prayer owner, two linked Latin phrases.
Petition for the fire of divine love and eternal charity while returning thurible; in Guéranger's Solemn Mass description this is to the deacon; priest/minister action varies by Mass form.

Faithful assent to priest's invitation and benefit of same sacrifice; spiritual participation not equal to ministerial sacramental consecration; server/priest grammatical variants should be form-gated.

hardHolds: Existing 955 parent evidence attachments are not proofs of precise word-level interpretation; do not relabel author claims in 42-pair workbook without direct citation.
This Guéranger historical source is one text witness supplementing the existing evidence; do not create 32 new canonical publications or author IDs.
Latin cue existence is confirmed, but 435 micro-unit subdivisions are not automatically exact runtime word spans. Existing split-boundary U003 in AO.V3.0226 and AO.V3.0227 starts with a comma.
Liturgical conclusion formulas do not need new individual exegesis.
Do not infer a deacon at Low Mass or confuse the priest's incense action with a universal faithful posture.
Do not promote Guéranger's symbolic reading of commixture to new sacramental consecration, nor his possible historical liturgical judgments to universal 1962 law.
Scripture cited in a discussion of a prayer should be attached at discussion/source scope until its exact clause is editorially verified.
Guéranger and Catholic Catechism sources give different publication dates and authority classes; never merge their identities.
No new author-specific Scripture columns should be populated as if authored by an uncited authority.
